source_solver: gurobipy 13.0.3 (Gurobi Optimizer 13.0.3, size-limited pip licence); original notebook railway_dispatching.ipynb code cells run unmodified via exec (dataset = 'linear', the notebook default; %pip and plotting cells dropped) on 2026-11-02
notes: Gurobi reports ObjVal 46.999992004792375 (a big-M tolerance artefact of the true optimum 47), status optimal, NumVars 218 (32 entry times + 6 finish times + 180 binaries), NumConstrs 367, NumIntVars 180 (all binary). HiGHS, SCIP and CBC all return 47. The notebook ships three datasets; 'linear' (its default, 6 trains on 4 stations and 3 single tracks) matches the shortlist size. The others give yshape 153 (548 vars / 1015 rows) and xshape 25 (519 / 1028) but are not ported. Notebook bug, reproduced: M = sum(duration) * len(trains) sums the dict KEYS (resource ids 0..6 = 21), not the durations, so M = 21 * 6 = 126 instead of the intended 29 * 6 = 174. The port computes M the same way (sum of resource ids times the number of trains). On the base data M = 126 is not binding (M = 10000 also gives 47), but for scenarios with much longer times a time gap above M is cut off. Reformulation: none. Same variables and rows in the same groups; the notebook's 'first event UB = 0' becomes lowBound = upBound = trains.ready_time, which is 0 for every train in the base data. The new ready_time column is the delay surface (a train that can enter its first resource only later). Alternative optima: total_delay and trains_delayed (4: A, B, E, F) are unique. last_arrival (49..52), max_train_delay (20..23) and the delays of A, B and F are not, and neither is the meet binary x (it can be 1 even when y would also hold).
